newsitem.title: UK: Mirror, News boost UK PA stakes.
newsitem.headline: Mirror, News boost UK PA stakes.

text.p: Mirror Group and News International have lifted their stakes in the UK's Press Association (PA) to around 19 and 13 percent respectively, PA chief executive Robert Simpson said on Thursday.
"I can confirm that the sales have taken place," said Simpson.

News International, the UK arm of Rupert Murdoch's News Corp, acquired an 11 percent stake from Canada's Thomson Corp and around two percent from Home Counties Newspapers. It previously had only a nominal stake in the PA, Britain's domestic news agency.
Mirror Group lifted its stake from 17 percent to 19 percent by buying shares from a number of non-media investors. The price of the sales was not disclosed.
Daily Mail and General Trust, which has 14 percent and United News & Media, with 11 percent, are the other two main shareholders.
Simpson would not comment on speculation that the new ownership structure effectively ruled out a mooted flotation.

"The charter for the PA is to make it an exciting, interesting and commercially successful company," he said, adding that the shareholders would address the question of a flotation as and when they thought it an issue.
